verification.runtime_check: Ran the real app on a temp db/uploads with uvicorn, and drove it with headless Chrome over CDP (Node 22 WebSocket). - Create textarea maxlength attr = 200. Input.insertText of 250 chars -> value length 200. 150 emoji (300 UTF-16 units) -> 200 UTF-16 units = 100 emoji, so the browser stops at 100 emoji while the server would accept 200 (the recorded, expected UTF-16 vs code-point difference). - Forced POST 422 via Fetch.fulfillRequest: #form-error visible with the exact expected message. - Edit: seeded a 300-char post directly in the TEMP db. Opening Edit shows the full 300-char text in the textarea (maxlength does not truncate a programmatically set value). Clicking Save unchanged sends 300 chars and the real server returns 422; the edit form stays open with "Couldn't update your log: description must be at most 200 characters. Shorten your description to 200 characters or fewer and try again." The user must shorten the text to save. Typing 250 chars over a selection yields 200. After replacing with short text, Save closes the form and reloads the list. - Forced PUT 422 shows the same message in .edit-error. Servers and the verifier's Chrome were stopped (ports 8765 and 9333 no longer listening). A broad "kill all chrome.exe" was denied by the permission system and not used; only my own processes (matched by the scratchpad profile path) were stopped.
verification.real_data_check: Read-only (mode=ro) open of the real logs.db: 1 row, 0 descriptions over 200 characters (max trimmed length 11). So no existing real post is blocked from editing by the new limit.
verification.file_integrity: md5 of every non-.claude, non-.venv file before vs after my run: identical (diff clean), and no file newer than my snapshot, so my run created no new files or caches in the project. backend/__pycache__ and backend/tests/__pycache__ already existed before my run (pytest was run with -p no:cacheprovider and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1). I had no git baseline, so I could not diff the touched files against their pre-change versions; I could only confirm the five touched files contain the described changes and that nothing outside them is newer.
verification.self_critique: Not tested: other browsers, the Docker path, IME or paste behaviour beyond insertText, and the real (not forced) 422 on the create form (the server 422 path was covered by the edit Save and by HTTP, but the create toast used a forced response). The pre-existing over-200 post behaviour (edit shows the long text and Save is rejected until shortened) is an observed consequence, not a defect against the spec. Chrome CDP timing used fixed sleeps. Whether the touched-file edits are the only ones made since the task began cannot be proven without a baseline.
